controller_deadline_model.classification_rule: Expiry before the accept frame and expiry after it are distinct phases (RELEASE_ACCEPT_DEADLINE_EXPIRED, RELEASE_COMPLETION_DEADLINE_EXPIRED) but both are RELEASE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, because in either case the helper may already have written the gate.  NOT_RELEASED is produced only where the protocol proves non-release: a terminal first frame, a reported write failure, or a release request that was never put on the wire at all.
controller_deadline_model.enforcement: absolute monotonic deadline owned by the controller process, applied to each socket operation and restored afterwards
controller_deadline_model.helper_bypass: After a helper deadline the controller stops asking: it signals the launcher through its own pidfd, kills and reaps the helper it forked, and reaps the launcher the kernel reparented to it.  The local cgroup kill domain runs first and never waits on the helper.
controller_deadline_model.no_process_wide_timer: No signal.alarm, setitimer, or SIGALRM handler exists anywhere in the package; a process-wide timer would corrupt unrelated operations.  A test asserts their absence.
controller_deadline_model.nominal_latency: Nominal effects take the same path as before: a healthy helper answers well inside every deadline, and no additional round trip was introduced.
controller_deadline_model.poisoned_connection: A deadline that expires mid-frame destroys the length-prefixed framing, so the connection is marked broken and every later call refuses immediately.  A wedged helper therefore costs one deadline in total rather than one per remaining call.

current_validation_artifact_model.rationale: The superseded bytes are preserved unchanged under a clearly historical filename, and the canonical filename carries the single current report, so third-party tooling never has to decide which of two files is authoritative.

diagnosed_root_causes.M2-B32: SpawnedLauncher.release() retained only a RELEASED outcome and rebuilt every other answer from _awaiting_release, which the first call had already cleared.  A first call returning RELEASE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN / EXECUTION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN was therefore followed by NOT_RELEASED / NO_INSTRUCTION_EXECUTED -- a positive claim that the proposed command never ran, made by a controller that never had that evidence.
diagnosed_root_causes.M2-B33: Every helper round trip was a blocking recv on a socket with no timeout: the release accept and completion frames, kill, wait, poll, spawn, startup, and the shutdown exchange in failure cleanup.  abort_gated_effect called helper-mediated kill(), wait() and poll() synchronously, so a helper that was alive but wedged, stopped, or protocol-deadlocked held the trusted controller open indefinitely -- before release classification, before local cgroup cleanup, and before any refusal evidence existed.  The helper's own wait timeout is a promise from the failing component, not a bound.
diagnosed_root_causes.M2-B34: The mount-namespace helper forks the launcher, so the launcher is the controller's grandchild and the controller cannot wait() on it.  When the helper died after the gate write, cgroup.kill still destroyed the domain and an empty cgroup.procs still proved no live member -- but neither fact says who observed the exit or who reaped it.  The abort evidence collapsed 'the domain was killed' into launcher_reaped, and the prior physical test never asserted launcher_reaped while the reports claimed the reap succeeded.
diagnosed_root_causes.M2-B35: _members_of() mapped an unreadable cgroup.procs to set(), making 'membership unreadable' and 'membership observed empty' the same value.  Bootstrap parent depopulation, manager membership verification, cached-topology revalidation, probe emptiness, attach verification, kill-domain enumeration, quiescence, and removal eligibility are all decisions about emptiness, and every one of them read a failed read as a positive answer.
diagnosed_root_causes.M2-M36: implementation/M2_VALIDATION_REPORT.json carried the final 379-test count semantics and two B25 closure objects recording a 125-test delegated run, while its top-level fields still said terminal_verdict=M2_FOURTH_CRITICAL_REPAIRS_REFUSED, cgroup_delegation_available=false, real_delegated_cgroup_qualification=false, and IMPLEMENTED_NOT_PHYSICALLY_QUALIFIED for M2-B25/EXEC-06.  One current artifact asserted a physical qualification and its absence.

constraints_preserved: no untrusted command becomes an uncontrolled child of the controller: the launcher only reparents here after the helper dies, and it is killed and reaped inside one bounded cleanup
no unrelated child is reaped: waitpid is only ever called on an owned PID and never on -1 or 0, which is_addressable_pid() enforces

rejected_alternatives.alternative: pidfd alone, with waitid(P_PIDFD) from the non-parent controller
rejected_alternatives.rejected_because: waitid(P_PIDFD) on a non-child fails with ECHILD; this was physically confirmed rather than assumed.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: let the controller fork the launcher directly instead of the helper
rejected_alternatives.rejected_because: the launcher must run inside the helper's mount namespace; entering it from outside needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the owning user namespace, which an unprivileged controller does not have.  It would also destroy the private-tmpfs materialisation this milestone already qualified.

it adds a third trusted process with its own lifecycle, IPC, deadline, and failure modes to answer a question one process-wide flag already answers.  That is an orchestration framework, which this assignment forbids.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: treat an empty effect cgroup as proof of reap
rejected_alternatives.rejected_because: an empty cgroup proves no live member.  It is equally consistent with an unrelated ancestor having reaped the launcher and with a zombie this controller cannot see.  It is exactly the inference M2-B34 names as the defect.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: rely on init (PID 1) to reap the orphan
rejected_alternatives.rejected_because: an unrelated global init is invisible evidence: the controller could neither observe the reap nor name the reaper.

process_ownership_architecture.residual_disclosed: While the flag is held, an orphaned descendant of this controller that no effect owns would reparent here and is not reaped, because reaping it would require waitpid(-1) and could consume an unrelated child.  The window is bounded by helper lifetime.
process_ownership_architecture.statement: The trusted controller calls prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, 1) before forking the mount-namespace helper.  When the helper dies, the kernel reparents the orphaned launcher to the nearest subreaper ancestor -- this controller -- so waitpid on that exact PID is a reap this process performed and can name.  A pidfd opened on the launcher supplies exit observation independently of parentage.  Exit observation and reap remain two separately recorded facts.

subreaper_lifecycle.acquired: immediately before the first trusted helper is forked, in PrivateMountHelper.start
subreaper_lifecycle.controller_shutdown: PrivateExecutionView.close -> PrivateMountHelper.close releases the acquisition on every path, including the failure paths in start()
subreaper_lifecycle.fork_safety: the acquisition records its owner PID; a copy inherited across fork() is discarded rather than trusted, because the kernel flag is not inherited
subreaper_lifecycle.readback: the flag is read back after being set; a write that reports success while the kernel disagrees is refused, not believed
subreaper_lifecycle.reference_counted: one activation shared by concurrent effects, each helper holding one acquisition
subreaper_lifecycle.restored: the previous flag value is restored when the last helper closes

verified_kernel_semantics: waitid(P_PIDFD, ...) on a process that is not the caller's child fails with ECHILD, so a pidfd alone never grants the right to reap.  Asserted by KernelOwnershipSemanticsTests::test_a_pidfd_alone_does_not_permit_a_non_parent_to_reap.
PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER is not inherited across fork(), so the helper does not become a subreaper and the launcher reparents past it to the controller.
A pidfd becomes readable when the process terminates, whether or not the reader is its parent, which is why it can carry exit observation but not reap.
process_ownership_architecture.why_smallest: It changes no part of the launch topology.  The helper still forks the launcher, so the private mount namespace still materialises the tmpfs by a helper-local pathname and the gate-before-exec ordering, membership verification before release, and cgroup kill-domain semantics are all untouched.  One process-wide flag with an owned lifetime is the entire mechanism.

release_state_monotonicity_evidence.evidence_layer: abort_gated_effect reads the launcher's own terminal outcome through monotonic_release_truth, so a caller that hands in a stronger outcome at cleanup time cannot overwrite what the launcher already established.
release_state_monotonicity_evidence.interim_phase: RELEASE_NOT_REQUESTED, which is never recorded as terminal
release_state_monotonicity_evidence.invariant: A release attempt that produced NOT_RELEASED, RELEASED, or RELEASE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN has answered the question terminally.  Every later call and every durable record repeats that outcome.

typed_membership_evidence.members_accessor: EffectCgroup.members() raises CgroupMembershipUnreadable rather than returning an empty set, so no caller can receive a bare empty set on a failed read.
typed_membership_evidence.opaque_members: The kernel renders cgroup.procs in the reader's PID namespace and prints 0 for a member that namespace cannot name.  Physical inspection of this host's root cgroup found 207 such entries.  A 0 is neither a PID nor noise: it is a live member this controller cannot address.  It is counted separately, it defeats emptiness, and it is never signalled individually.
